lines.text: Here's a question about a set of company filings. Every company and person in them is made up.
Plain RAG searches the filings, and says the answer isn't there.
It is there. It's just split across three documents.
One says who runs Cahaya Teguh.
Another names her spouse.
A third says which board that spouse chairs.
NEXUS turns the filings into a graph first.
Ask again, with hybrid search alongside. Hybrid still comes back empty.
Graph local takes about twenty seconds, because it walks the graph.
From Cahaya Teguh, to its Direktur Utama, Zaenab Thamrin.
Then to her spouse, Raden Prasasta.
Then to PT Karya Semesta,
where Raden Prasasta has been Komisaris Utama since 2019.
Every hop cites its sentence. Open one, and there's the source.
Explore opens the same graph by hand. This is Zaenab Thamrin's neighbourhood.
Themes groups it into communities, each with a written summary.
On 112 answerable questions, graph local matched the gold answer 70% of the time.
Hybrid, 52%.
The paired difference is +0.18, with a 95% interval from +0.09 to +0.28.
It doesn't win everything.
On thematic questions, hybrid leads, 0.84 to 0.66.
Underneath: Neo4j, Milvus and Postgres, with LangGraph, FastAPI and Next.js.
All of it runs on your machine. The code is on GitHub.
